summaryText:
Pastor Travis Hearn opened the new five-week series My Wounds Won't Win with a message titled I Am Not My Wounds. After a warm welcome and worship, he reminded the church that everyone has been hurt in some way, and that some of the deepest wounds are invisible, hidden behind smiles, success, or busyness. His concern was that unhealed wounds can quietly shape how we see ourselves, how we treat others, and how we face the future. Drawing on Psalm 147:3, he reminded the congregation that Jesus came not only to forgive sin but also to heal the brokenhearted and bind up their wounds.

The message centered on John 5, where Jesus meets a man who had been unable to walk for 38 years near the pool of Bethesda. Pastor Travis noted that the man is never named and is described only by his condition. He invited listeners to ask what names they have been carrying that Jesus never gave them. He also spoke of a real spiritual battle over identity (Ephesians 6) and said that while we cannot choose what happens to us, we can choose whether our wounds win.

He shared three keys. First, Jesus gives us a new identity. People and culture may label us by our failures or pain, but Jesus calls us by our purpose, and Scripture calls believers chosen, loved, forgiven, and a new creation. Second, Jesus invites us to leave our old identity behind. His question to the man, "Do you want to get well?", was about more than the man's legs. It asked whether he was ready to leave a life built around his condition. Third, Jesus calls us to walk in our new identity. When Jesus told the man to pick up his mat and walk, Pastor Travis explained, it showed that God does not erase our history but redeems it, so that what once defined us becomes a testimony and a witness to God's grace.

The service closed with an invitation to receive Jesus as Savior, a prayer of salvation, and prayer for those carrying wounds such as shame, guilt, unforgiveness, fear, and addiction. The prayer team was available at the front, and online viewers were encouraged to share their decisions through the QR code. Church leaders also encouraged everyone to commit to all five weeks, invite someone to join them, and consider giving through the Impact Church app. The hopeful message throughout was that what happened to us does not have the final word, because Jesus gives us a new name.
mainPoints: Jesus gives me a new identity: He calls us by our purpose and not by our injury, and the labels of the world and the enemy do not define us.
Jesus invites me to leave my old identity: Like the man at the pool, we are asked "Do you want to get well?" and invited to walk away from a life built around our wounds.
Jesus calls me to walk in my new identity: God redeems our history so that our wounds become testimony and witness instead of identity.

Here a great number of disabled people used to lie: the blind, the lame, the paralyzed. One who was there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years. When Jesus saw him lying there and learned that he had been in this condition for a long time, he asked him, "Do you want to get well?" "Sir," the invalid replied, "I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am trying to get in, someone else goes down ahead of me." Then Jesus said to him, "Get up! Pick up your mat and walk." At once the man was cured; he picked up his mat and walked.

Monday.scripture: Psalm 147:3 (NIV): "He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds."
Monday.focus: Being honest with God about the places that still hurt.
Monday.action: Set aside ten quiet minutes. Write down one wound or label you have been carrying, then read Psalm 147:3 aloud over it.
Monday.prayer: Lord Jesus, You see every hurt I have carried. I bring them to You honestly today. Heal my heart and bind up my wounds. Amen.

Tuesday.scripture: 2 Corinthians 5:17 (NIV): "Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!"
Tuesday.focus: Receiving the new identity Jesus gives.
Tuesday.action: Write three identity statements from Scripture, such as chosen, loved, and forgiven. Place them where you will see them today and read them aloud.
Tuesday.prayer: Father, thank You for calling me Your child. Help me believe the name You have spoken over me more than any label I have carried. Amen.

Wednesday.scripture: John 5:6 (NIV): "When Jesus saw him lying there and learned that he had been in this condition for a long time, he asked him, 'Do you want to get well?'"
Wednesday.focus: Answering Jesus' question and being willing to leave the old identity behind.
Wednesday.action: Notice one phrase you often say about yourself, like "I'm just..." or "I'll never...". Write a truthful, Scripture-based replacement and use it today.
Wednesday.prayer: Jesus, yes, I want to be well. Show me any place where I have built my life around my pain, and give me courage to leave it behind. Amen.

Thursday.scripture: Ephesians 6:12 (NIV): "For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms."
Thursday.focus: Standing on God's truth when old labels try to return.
Thursday.action: When a negative thought about who you are shows up today, pause and speak one truth from Scripture about who God says you are. Pray briefly before moving on.
Thursday.prayer: Lord, thank You that I do not fight alone. Guard my mind and heart, and help me stand on what You say about me. Amen.

Friday.scripture: John 5:8 (NIV): "Then Jesus said to him, 'Get up! Pick up your mat and walk.'"
Friday.focus: Walking out the new identity with one step of obedience.
Friday.action: Choose one practical step toward healing, such as forgiving someone in prayer, reaching out to a trusted friend, or asking a pastor or counselor for support.
Friday.prayer: Jesus, You have told me to get up and walk. Give me strength for the next step, and help me trust You as I take it. Amen.

Saturday.scripture: James 5:16 (NIV): "Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective."
Saturday.focus: Letting God turn our story into testimony and encouraging others.
Saturday.action: Pray with or for someone today. Share one way God has been faithful to you, or invite a friend to join this series next Sunday.
Saturday.prayer: God, thank You that my story is part of Your story. Use what You are healing in me to bring hope to someone else. Amen.

title: How to Heal from Emotional Wounds Without Letting Them Define You | I Won't Let My Wounds Win Pt. 1
